#889. Arsenal dig deep to earn WCL draw in face of Barcelona dominance

Arsenal continue to be a sharp thorn in the side of the European champions, Barcelona, and they dug deep to hold on to a draw at the Camp Nou on Thursday night. Frida Maanum put the Gunners ahead despite a hugely dominant performance from Barcelona, but Caroline Graham Hansen’s equaliser ensured the spoils would be shared.

Barcelona have been formidable when playing at the club’s main stadium, winning nine and drawing twice, against Chelsea in the semi-finals in 2023 and now Arsenal.

“Grit, resilience, discipline, clarity, communication, leadership, bravery – that’s a lot of words,” said Renée Slegers, whose side now lie fourth in the standings. “There’s a lot of really good things in this performance that we definitely want to build on.”

The last time these two teams met, Arsenal lifted the Champions League trophy at Barcelona’s expense after the most perfect defensive performance and a Stina Blackstenius goal in Lisbon in 2025. It was a far less perfect defensive performance this time but Arsenal showed the guts they have been missing at times this season, against the team that retook their crown last season, and showed they can play ugly when needed.

There was one change to the team that earned a 2-1 win against Liverpool on Sunday, but it was a significant one. Olivia Smith was replaced by Maanum and the Norwegian slotted into the No 10 role with Alessia Russo, who has scored 12 goals in nine games for club and country, moving into the centre-forward position.

It was the England forward’s play on the left that set up the shock first-half goal that temporarily silenced the crowd. She beat two and worked the ball to Maanum. Barcelona got the ball away but Russo was there again and delivered a perfect cross across the face of goal for Caitlin Foord. The Australian forced a close-range save from Cata Coll only for Maanum to power in the loose ball.

The pocket of travelling fans behind plexiglass in the upper tier were jubilant. About 1,000 had travelled despite the late switch of the match to Thursday due to a 24-hour general strike in Spain on Wednesday.

Benfica rebounded from their humbling defeat by Arsenal last time out to claim a second Women’s Champions League victory of the season by seeing off struggling Austria Vienna 3-1.

Beaten 3-0 at Meadow Park a fortnight ago following Alessia Russo’s hat-trick, Benfica had the ideal opportunity to get back to winning ways against a Vienna side who had picked up one point in three games.

They went ahead at Lisbon’s Estadio da Luz through Andreia Norton in the fifth minute before Carina Wenninger levelled after half-time when Valentina Potzl was upended in the area by Lena Pauels.

But Vienna goalkeeper Jasmin Pal’s 73rd-minute red card proved a turning point as Caroline Møller headed home before she teed up Nycole Raysla to score in time added on. Press Association

The goal came decidedly against the run of play but Barcelona struggled to capitalise on their first-half dominance. Ewa Pajor and Graham Hansen were particularly threatening as Barcelona targeted Arsenal’s left, made up of the less experienced Taylor Hinds and Lisa Baum.

The scoreline at the break was a little unfathomable based on the run of play and the domestic fortunes of both sides. While Arsenal languish in sixth in the WSL, 12 points behind the league leaders, Manchester City, Barcelona have won nine of their 10 games in Liga F, having scored 41 goals and built a five-point lead over their nearest rivals, Real Madrid.

Arsenal’s gameplan felt familiar. It was as if they had studied the blueprint religiously followed by teams that have sat back in a low block and frustrated them week-in, week-out in the WSL this season.

No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football

Aitana Bonmatí, the three-time Ballon d’Or winner, was surprisingly relegated to the bench but her arrival shortly before the hour elevated Barcelona’s threat, causing Arsenal’s defending to look even more calamitous at times, and lifted the mood in a frustrated stadium.

Three minutes after her arrival they were level. Esmee Brugts found an unmarked Graham Hansen on the right and she cut inside and swept in past Misa Rodríguez.

It was no surprise that Baum and Hinds, who had been run ragged, were removed soon after, with former Barcelona player Ona Batlle and Smith, Arsenal’s record signing, replacing them.

Arsenal were better after the goal and the changes, occasionally breaking free of their prison of a final third. At the end they were clinging on, but cling on they did.

“If we were to do it again, we’d try to stay on the ball for longer and play our game even more,” said Slegers. “Definitely there were moments in the first half and in the second half where we were really, really dangerous and created big chances, open chances. I’m just really pleased with the way we played the game tonight because it’s a very different game to what we usually play and that we can do it this way is a big boost for us as a team and that’s what we’re going to take with us going forward.”

#888. Julianne Hough Reacts to Derek Hough’s Sister-to-Lover Moment on DWTS

After Derek Hough reacted to fellow Dancing With the Stars judge Carrie Ann Inaba’s viral sister-to-lover comment on the show, his sister Julianne Hough shared her response.

An awkward moment on Dancing With the Stars basically left Julianne Hough thinking, “Oh, brother.”

The DWTS co-host reacted to a cringey moment from the Nov. 10 episode when her brother—and judge on the competition series—Derek Hough made a quip about sibling dynamics.

ICYMI, after Paralympian Ezra Frech and his pro partner Daniella Karagach, who have detailed their sibling-like relationship this season, performed a sensual Argentine tango, they received some shocking praise from judge Carrie Ann Inaba.

“You were able to stay so centered on yourself while also delivering the story that I want so much with this dance,” she said. “The intimacy, turning your sister into your lover for one night is all good.”

As Ezra and Daniella were left in surprise, co-host Alfonso Ribeiro said, “Sister lover, that’s awkward.” And as the mic was turned over to Derek, he quipped with laughter, “Tell me about it. That was weird.”

The moment prompted a flurry of comments online, as fans pointed out how Julianne and Derek have been paired up for some sensual dances over the years. As one fan wrote on Threads, “Derek adding in ‘tell me about it’ after Carrie Ann gave Ezra and Daniella credit for doing an intimate dance when they feel like siblings had me GIGGGGGGGLING.”

After all, the 38-year-old only added a shrugging emoji while sharing a Thread post to her Instagram Stories Nov. 12 that read, “Derek adding in ‘tell me about it’ after Carrie Ann gave Ezra and Daniella credit for doing an intimate dance when they feel like siblings had me GIGGGGGGGLING.”

But Julianne appeared to sidestep the awkwardness with one smooth move. After all, the 38-year-old re-posted the comment on her Instagram Story and simply added a shrugging emoji to prove her nonchalance.

But while Julianne may have shimmied away from this week’s snafu, it’s not the first sibling-centric shuffle that Carrie Ann has caused between her and Derek. In fact, after Carrie Ann paired them up in 2014 for an intimate routine, fans thought the Houghs were married.

“Our first thing that we ever did on Dancing with the Stars was the live tour,” Julianne said on a September 2025 episode of the Chicks in the Office podcast. “Carrie Ann was the one who choreographed everything, and she got us to do a rumba together. You guys, that’s the dance of love that my brother and I had to dance together.”

“Our names in the program were ‘Derek and Julianne Hough,’ so everybody thought we were married and were doing this rumba,” Julianne continued. “When people found out we were brother and sister? I remember there was one venue, and we just heard, ‘That’s just wrong!’”

For a deeper dive into the siblings’—yes, siblings’—family tree, keep reading…

The Hough family patriarch is originally from Coeur d’Alene, Idaho, and met future wife Mariann Heaton on the ballroom team at Ricks College (now Brigham Young University-Idaho).

Bruce and Mariann—both from Mormon families and the children of ballroom-dancing parents—settled in Salt Lake City. There he worked as a communications executive and co-founded supplement maker Nutraceutical Corporation, which, according to Deseret News, reached a valuation of $300 million under his watch before it was sold in 2017.

Bruce also ventured into politics, serving two terms as state Republican Party chair and running for congress in 2023.

While he didn't win that race, he told Deseret News at the time that he was running for his family's future. "I’ve got 10 kids, I’ve got 22 grandkids and growing," he explained. "And I really feel that America’s promise is in jeopardy for those grandkids especially."

Of his most famous offspring, he quipped, "I never thought that those dance lessons would pay off,” noting that he took the most pride in hearing from others that son Derek Hough and daughter Julianne Hough were some of the "kindest people…in the entertainment business.”

In addition to Derek and Julianne, Bruce shares daughters Sharee Hough Selman, Marabeth Poole and Katherine Hough with Mariann. After they divorced in the late 1990s, he married Debra Francom Hough, also a parent of five.

Mariann grew up in Idaho Falls with three brothers.

She and Bruce were in the process of divorcing when Julianne and Derek, then 10 and 13, moved to London to attend the Italia Conti Academy of Theatre Arts.

Their leaving was "devastating," Mariann recalled on a 2019 episode of The Minds Gym podcast. But they wanted to dance and, she explained, "The biggest thing that kept me going is that I grew up feeling very dominated over and controlled. Love my parents, but that was like a generational thing."

However, she added, "I'm grateful for that now because…it made me sway to I love having free agency." It was also "so important" for her to pass that on to her kids, she said, and "all of them are so not afraid to go travel and do all these things."

Mariann, now based in Franklin, Tenn., is a painter and has credited husband Aaron Nelson for supporting and encouraging her work as an artist.

Sharee married husband Mark Selman when she was 19 and they share six kids.

The eldest of Bruce and Mariann's brood danced at Ballet West in Utah and these days runs her own fitness business, Hough Werks, teaching yoga and dance.

Her "dynamic" firstborn "just came into this world with a lot of energy," Mariann said on The Minds Gym. Sharee's "little mind was just going all the time, just super creative" and "self-motivated."

Moreover, with 11 years between Sharee and her youngest sister, "Julianne thinks she has two moms."

Marabeth is "just a beautiful spirit" who "loves her own space," Mariann said of her second child, and she "puts on these little retreats in Nashville for women."

She left Utah for Music City to "be a country star," baby sister Julianne shared on the Not Skinny but Not Fat podcast in September 2025, and now makes the most of her positive energy as a realtor and holistic health coach, as well as a singer-songwriter.

Marabeth married Michael Poole in 2002 and they live in Nashville with son Aidan.

Daughter Katherine, a mother of three, "just makes you smile," Mariann said on The Minds Gym, "and she's just real."

The esthetician was in a relationship with Tony Schnur before his death from brain cancer in 2023. "It’s unfair that I found my soulmate, my best friend, my partner in life, only to lose you too soon," Katherine posted on Instragram in February 2025, marking the second anniversary of his passing. "I miss you every day."

But Katherine has persevered, Julianne gushing on Not Skinny But Not Fat, "She has three beautiful daughters and she has all these activities and she plans all these things, and I'm in awe of her."

And on Sept. 24, 2025, Katherine shared that she had found love again, writing on Instagram alongside a montage of sweet photos, "After walking through so much loss and heartache, I never imagined I’d find this kind of love again. Chris is the man I prayed for, kind, generous, loving, patient, and such a gift not only to me but to my girls."

Born May 17, 1985, Derek joined Dancing With the Stars as a pro in 2007. He won the Mirrorball Trophy a record six times and is a four-time Emmy winner for choreography.

After his last competitive turn around the floor in 2016, Derek returned to DWTS as a fulltime judge in 2020.

He met fellow dancer Hayley Erbert in 2015 and, after navigating some "insane obstacles," as he put it on Couple Things With Shawn Johnson and Andrew East, they got married in August 2023.

As a couple they powered through Hayley's life-threatening health scare, a brain hemorrhage that required emergency surgery just four months after their wedding, and in July 2025 they announced they were expecting their first child together.

Posting a photo of dad Bruce dancing at his and Hayley's wedding, Derek wrote on Facebook in April 2024, "Smart, kind and thoughtful. I hope to be as good as a father as he has been to his family."

The baby of the Hough family was born July 20,1988. She joined DWTS in 2007 along with Derek and proceeded to win her first two seasons on the show.

She left in 2009 to pursue acting and scored a breakthrough role in 2010's Burlesque (though her big-screen debut was actually playing an unnamed Hogwarts student in 2001's Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone) before scoring the lead in the 2011 Footloose remake. Julianne returned to the ballroom as a judge from 2014 to 2017, winning an Emmy for choreography along the way, and has cohosted DWTS with Alfonso Ribeiro since 2023.

Julianne married Brooks Laich in 2017 but they split up in 2020, eventually finalizing their divorce in 2022.

She said on The Jamie Kern Lima Show in 2024 that going through a divorce gave her a chance to "reconnect" with her mom and dad, and they "showed up" for her.

"I needed that," Julianne explained. "I reclaimed my parental relationship with them and I got to be the kid and they got to take care of me. And that was the most healing [thing]."

Reflecting on her and Derek becoming the stars of the family, Julianne said on Not Skinny But Not Fat that there was "no jealousy" between their other siblings, "but there is a sadness that maybe there wasn't an opportunity for them to experience it."

Sharee, Marabeth and Katherine are "so, so, so happy," Julianne continued. "They have great lives, and they love their life. But we had an opportunity that they didn't have, and it's hard.”

And while she and Derek have a special connection, "they were super close as sisters growing up,” Julianne said. “So, I didn't get to have the closeness of sisters and that bond. [And] they have marriages and kids and I don't have that experience."

Meanwhile, all five siblings "get along really well," Mariann said on The Minds Gym. "I think the hard part is being away from each other, because there is some kind of a synergy when they all get together."

#887. 'Memories flood back' - Rochdale & York meet again after title drama

Rochdale and York City meet for the first time since last season's dramatic title decider

It is just over six months since one of the greatest games to decide a title.

Rochdale and York City had clinched a huge 212 points between them heading into an extraordinary final-day showdown at Crown Oil Arena on 25 April.

In the end, York City clinched automatic promotion from the National League by the barest of margins, snatching a 1-1 draw courtesy of Josh Stones' stunning equaliser in the 13th minute of stoppage time.

Having ensured promotion in dramatic circumstances of their own through a tough play-off campaign, Rochdale joined them in League Two this term, with the pair facing each other for the first time since their epic fixture.

Plenty has changed for both clubs as they adapt to life back in the English Football League (EFL).

How are both clubs faring this season? And will they forever be linked by that historic day?

Josh Stones scored his 18th league goal of the season to secure the title for York

Saturday, 25 April 2026 will live long in the memory of not just both sets of supporters but neutrals as well, with fans across the world choosing to follow a fifth-tier football match on a busy day's action in late April.

The game came to life in the final stages. After York had spurned a fantastic opportunity to open the scoring late on through Stones, Rochdale fans inside the ground began to sense luck may be on their side.

Not least when Ian Henderson, Rochdale's cult hero, swung in a peach of a cross with the outside of his foot which was headed home at the far post by Emmanuel Dieseruvwe in the 95th minute.

Cue bedlam. Rochdale fans stormed the pitch in pure elation and emotion. They thought they were promoted.

"As a local radio commentator you want to capture what fans are feeling. As Emmanuel Dieseruvwe headed in on the 95th minute, myself and former Rochdale player Joe Bunney went big," BBC Radio Manchester commentator Alex Whitington said.

"It felt like that was the moment. We stood up to describe the pitch invasion and stayed standing to call Dale home."

But that gave the York players, and management staff, time to reset. More than six minutes passed between Rochdale's goal and York restarting the match. The visitors still believed.

In the 13th minute of stoppage time, Stones made no mistake with his second opportunity of the game, managing to squeeze the ball over the line following pinball in the penalty area - sending York up with virtually the final kick of the season.

"There was a split-second moment when then Rochdale boss Jimmy McNulty thought the referee had blown the whistle for full-time, only to find out that in fact the whistle meant his side were staying in the National League - momentarily," BBC Radio York's Dave Ward said.

Whitington added: "Stones' equaliser was bedlam. Not least because from our angle it wasn't clear if the ball had crossed the line.

"I cried 'oh no' four times. I think that encapsulates the emotion perfectly. I may never commentate on another ending like it."

Rochdale were forced into the play-offs where they eventually produced another comeback, this time against Boreham Wood at Wembley to seal their EFL return.

"The supporters can't wait to get back - they will love the banter. The rivalry between the fans will be brilliant and all those memories will come flooding back," Ward added.

York win promotion with 103rd-minute equaliser at Rochdale

Their day, until it wasn't - the title decider that had it all

National League champions York City decided to make the unusual move of swapping managers in the summer despite their last-gasp title win.

Stuart Maynard departed the club in July and was replaced by former Crawley boss Scott Lindsey the following day - a move met with anger by many supporters at the time.

After an unbeaten run of five league matches between September and October, Lindsey's reign in North Yorkshire is now beginning to take shape and the Minstermen are inside the play-off places despite losing their past two games.

Last season's National League top scorer Ollie Pearce has continued to bang the goals in since stepping up to the EFL for the first time.

Pearce has scored eight in all competitions this season, including inside 10 seconds in York's 4-0 thumping of Northampton Town last Saturday in the FA Cup. It was the competition's third-quickest goal of all time.

The 31-year-old striker has been ably supported by Alex Newby in the absence of Stones who has struggled with injuries this campaign.

Attacking midfielder Newby has six league goals so far this term, and the returning Stones did get his name on the scoresheet during the win against the Cobblers.

Looking to Saturday's match, Lindsey underlined the importance of using the psychological advantage last season's final-day showdown might provide.

"The importance is the players feel that environment when they turn up at the stadium again. They will have good memories, so we'll definitely be leaning on that," Lindsey told BBC Radio York.

"I may mention about the last time they were there. It can only be a good thing what happened there last time."

Incredible radio commentary of York City's promotion-sealing goal

Rochdale also changed their manager in the summer - although their hand was rather more forced.

McNulty made the short journey to Stockport County and in came former South Shields boss Ian Watson.

Dale had a tough start to life back in the EFL after three years away and Watson was given a vote of confidence by the board in early September to give him time to turn the club's fortunes around.

It had an immediate effect. Rochdale drew with Walsall and then went on to beat local rivals Oldham Athletic and Fleetwood Town in their next three matches - yet Rochdale welcome their opponents on the back of a five-game winless run.

Last season's 27-goal striker Dieseruvwe is yet to find the net in the league this term and Rochdale are 13 places below Saturday's opponents, however, just five points separate them in a tightly packed League Two table after 14 matches.

Ian Henderson, at 41 years old, is continuing to cast his spell on the EFL.

Into his second stint at Spotland, and 13th season as a Rochdale player, Henderson has scored twice in his past three league games despite not yet starting a match.

While York have loftier ambitions, 22nd place or higher in Rochdale's first season back in the fourth tier come close of play on 8 May would represent a successful return to the EFL.

#886. Jamie Dornan & Anthony Mackie Share Hilarious Lesson From Fatherhood

Jamie Dornan and Anthony Mackie—who are costarring in the thriller series 12 12 12—exclusively told E! News about their kids' reactions to growing up with movie star dads.

Jamie Dornan and Anthony Mackie's most important critics are their kids.

The actors—who first starred in 2019's Synchronic before reuniting for upcoming TV series 12 12 12—confessed that amid their many roles as action stars over the years, earning cool points from their children has been no easy feat.

"If they don't think I'm cool after Lord of the Rings, I'm done," Dornan, who plays Aragorn in the upcoming prequel, The Hunt for Gollum, joked in an exclusive interview with E! News’ Will Marfuggi. "If that's not good enough for my kids, then I don't know what else to offer them."

The 50 Shades of Grey alum brought his three kids Dulcie, 13, Elva, 10 and Alberta, 7, with wife Amelia Warner to stay with him in New Zealand during the fantasy shoot, where they were thankfully impressed by his performance on set.

"Usually, they ask to leave. Like, they come to set, and after half an hour, they're like, 'You're just saying the same thing over and over. This is so boring,'" Dornan admitted. "They came to set one night when I was fighting and beheading orcs and stuff, and they were like, 'It was cool.'"

That said, the 44-year-old was pleased that his little ones found it "good to see Daddy all heroic like that" because, as he put it, "that'll be as cool as it gets for me."

Mackie's brood, on the other hand—which includes four sons with ex-wife Sheletta Chapital—weren't so easily won over by their dad moonlighting as a soldier with supernatural powers, but for good reason. The Captain America actor is already a superhero at home.

"My boys could care less," Mackie remarked with a laugh. "At the end of the day, I realized they just want me to be dad."

And the 48-year-old understands why his family unit is more content with quality time at home, including playing pickleball.

"I love the fact that all they want from me is me," he continued. "But then when I come home, we get to be one big family."

Still, Mackie admitted bringing the crew as his plus-fours to a red carpet was more than a typical 'bring your kids to work' day, even for them.

"They went to the premiere of my movie," Mackie recounted. "They had never seen anything of that scale, like of that magnitude."

And Mackie and Dornan's latest project is yet another grand production. The Marvel alum credited the art department when remarking, "The scale of the show, I feel, is kind of like another character."

The Belfast native agreed the ambitious approach paid off for the series, premiering Nov. 13 on Apple TV, about a meticulously planned fictional robbery of a bank in Zurich.

"It's like the biggest heist in European history," Dornan said, using the British slang for cheap when adding, "It couldn't be pony. It needed to be big."

New episodes drop on Fridays through Dec. 25.

#885. Missing Israel games 'stressful' for captain Collins

Collins is back for the final two Nations League games after missing the first four with a calf injury

Republic of Ireland captain Nathan Collins said he felt he left his team-mates "on their own" after missing the two controversial Nations League games against Israel in the last international window through injury.

Collins was sidelined for the four-game window in September and October with a calf problem and had to watch on as the Irish lost 1-0 away to Kosovo, beat Israel 3-0 in Debrecen and then draw 2-2 with Austria at home and 1-1 with Israel again in Serbia.

The first game against Israel in Hungary looked in doubt the previous day when training was delayed as players took a vote on whether to play - amid protests over the Israel-Gaza war - with goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu making himself unavailable for selection.

Back in the squad and speaking before Saturday's game away to Austria, the Brentford defender reflected on his personal disappointment at not being around to support his team-mates as captain during a testing time.

"It was probably more stressful away from it than it might have been in it," Collins said.

"I could only see what I could see online and it made it really tough. I didn't feel like I was afraid, but I felt I left the lads there on their own not being there, not being involved."

O'Shea proud of how team-mates handled Israel games

Republic of Ireland sit third in Group B3 and need two big performances in their last two games, against Austria in Linz and home to Kosovo on Tuesday, to have any chance of topping the group and earning promotion to League A.

Despite the challenges the Israel fixtures presented in the last window, Collins believes Heimir Hallgrimsson's squad are stronger coming out the other side of it and are now relishing the focus coming back to matters on the pitch.

"I just think everyone feels very comfortable around each other. I don't think anyone is shying away, I don't think anyone feels uncomfortable in the group," he continued.

"I just think everyone's really bonded well, there's a different feel to it. If anybody experienced what they went through, I think that's extremely normal.

"I think we will all go through a brick wall for each other. I can only keep emphasising that we're ready to go.

"I think we're excited to go and we want another game of football."

Head coach Hallgrimsson added that Seamus Coleman, who has been in the 24-man squad in a "hybrid" role, will not be considered for selection against Austria.

However, with Liam Scales, Jayson Molumby, Conor Coventry, Adam Idah and Ryan Manning all one yellow card away from suspension, the Icelander did not rule out the prospect of the 38-year-old featuring against Kosovo on Tuesday.

"No, we didn't expect to include him in the squad today," he said.

"On Tuesday, we don't know the situation. We can maybe answer that before that game or after this game. We have five players on a yellow."

Group leaders Austria are missing a number of key players for Saturday's game at Raiffeisen Arena through injury.

Nottingham Forest's Xaver Schlager and Hoffenheim's Alexander Prass, who scored in the draw in Dublin, are the latest to be ruled out.

Manager Ralf Rangnick is already without David Alaba, Maximilian Wober, Nikolas Veratschnig, Paul Wanner, Patrick Wimmer, Florian Grillitsch, Carney Chukwuemeka and Marco Grull for this window.

#883. Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame

David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025

David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class.

The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract.

He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield.

Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023.

His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas.

David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth Â£128m

He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey".

Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time."

Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility.

Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Womenâs World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019.

"To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram.

#881. Tearful Pochettino admits he 'couldn't say no to Man Utd'

Mauricio Pochettino has said leaving the United States to join Man Utd was the 'toughest decision of his career'; Pochettino will begin in his new role after he has led the USMNT in their two games against Haiti; the former Spurs boss has agreed a deal at Old Trafford until 2029

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

An emotional Mauricio Pochettino said that leaving his role with the United States was the "toughest decision of his career" but admitted he couldn't turn down the chance to become head coach of Manchester United.

Pochettino has been appointed as Michael Carrick's replacement at Old Trafford having signed a deal until the summer of 2029. It comes mere months after extending his stay with the USMNT until the 2030 World Cup.

The Argentine will begin his new role on November 18, after taking charge of the USA's two fixtures against Haiti.

Speaking in his pre-match press conference before his penultimate game, Pochettino broke down in tears as he explained his decision.

"In some part, this is a very sad decision. In another part, we are professionals. This is the next step to try and make your dreams come true," the former Spurs and Chelsea boss said.

"It all happened so quickly. By Sunday afternoon there was contact. You always were transparent and always tried to build something together. We learned a lot from you all, this amazing country and you amazing people. This is one of the most difficult decisions of my career. Thank you so much."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Pochettino last held a club role in Europe during his one-season stint at Chelsea, which came to an end in 2024. When asked why he had opted to leave his post to return to the Premier League, Pochettino didn't hide the fact that taking the Old Trafford hot seat was a once in a lifetime opportunity.

"It's obvious," Pochettino added. "They [US Soccer Federation] know that not many opportunities can happen in your career like a side the size of Manchester United.

"When that arrives, it's difficult to turn down."

Pochettino will start life at Carrington following the international break, and will have three training sessions with the players before the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool on Sunday, live on Sky Sports.

The new head coach admitted that he would have started sooner if asked to, but explained why he wanted to see out the remainder of this camp.

"I am a professional person and the emotional link between us we have built in this two years is to show the commitment and respect and care and love," Pochettino said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"Even if we take a decision which is not the best for one part, we've always been open. We have the respect of the players and staff, they understand the situation.

"Of course, if Manchester United and the federation agreed different terms, I would have respected between both. But this happened and of course, all the games are important.

"The last four games were important. We gave debuts to 13 players, before the cup I thought everyone had different ideas about it but we believe in the programme and are brave enough to go ahead. We're always optimistic and positive.

"After this camp, with four victories, we've been consistent in the same way, win or lose. We believe in the programme. It's an honour for us to be here, defend our patch and our players.

"We need to play tomorrow and the next game. We're not thinking in the future, it's about performing. We're very optimistic and it's a natural way to finish our partnership."

Follow Sky Sports on WhatsApp for the latest sports news, videos, features, analysis and much more

Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol:

"We've always known Mauricio Pochettino is an emotional person. He wears his heart on his sleeve. But I don't think you would normally expect a manager to break down and be so emotional in a press conference when he was leaving the USA to manage Manchester United.

"But that just tells you about the kind of guy he is because he's all about personal relationships. And obviously, he's made some very good friends in the US.

"He also said: 'We recovered our motivation here'. He was quite hurt and bruised by what happened to him at PSG and at Chelsea. It's almost like he's rediscovered his motivation by working in the US. And now he's ready to come back to the Premier League."

In the wake of the announcement of Pochettino as the new head coach at Old Trafford, his predecessor Michael Carrick penned an emotional farewell off the back of his sacking on Wednesday.

Carrick took to social media to thank supporters saying, “you've shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way".

In his post, the former Red Devils midfielder also lent an inadvertent word of advice for his replacement, giving an insight into what life is like at the club.

“To be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means,” Carrick added.

"It's different to anywhere else. Ultimately, you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time.

"It's a football club that's unique, with substance and history that cannot be ignored.”

#879. Special Forces Season 5 Finale: 3 Celebrity Winners Revealed

Special Forces: World’s Toughest Test crowned Candace Cameron Bure, Collin Gosselin and Alexia Umansky the season five winners, the celebrities outlasting the final competition.

These celebrities have proven they’re the world’s toughest.

While there were seven finalists heading into the Special Forces: World’s Toughest Test season five finale on Nov. 12, only three proved they truly had what it takes to win.

And those winners were: Candace Cameron Bure, Collin Gosselin and Alexia Umansky, who faced what one series staff sergeant called “12 hours of absolute hell” in order to ensure their victory.

The three winners, as well as boxer Alycia Baumgardner, French celebrity David Charvet, comedian Hannah Stocking and NBA alum Matt Barnes’ final challenge involved 12 hours of simulated interrogation after the finalists were “captured behind enemy lines.” They were tasked with devising and maintaining cover stories, building rapport and acting human with their captors, all while making it to the very end through hours of intense interrogation, the downtime of which they were kept in rooms with hoods on.

Baumgardner eventually pulled herself out of the challenge when the pressure became too much, Charvet was removed for failing to build rapport with his captors and Stocking and Barnes failed when interrogators were able to debunk their cover stories.

That left Jon & Kate Plus 8’s Gosselin, Umansky—who started the competition with her dad Mauricio Umansky—and Full House alum Bure, who proved they had what it took to win.

For Umansky, she shared how happy she was to bring home the win for her and her dad, adding she got through the toughest moments by keeping her eye on the prize.

“I have visualized what it’s like to walk out of this as a winner,” she said during a confessional. “I think I just have to keep that picture in my head so strong.”

Meanwhile, Bure felt her victory to have an impact beyond herself.

“This one’s for all the women out there,” she said through tears after winning. “No matter what challenges you have, physically you can do it.”

And for Gosselin—who is estranged from his mother Kate Gosselin and many of seven siblings, an ordeal he chronicles in his recently-released memoir—this show proved he was capable after previously being discharged from the Marines, which he alleges was orchestrated by his mother.

Through tears, the 22-year-old said, “Now I feel I have this new profound belief in myself that nobody can take away from me.”

But while Umansky, Gosselin and Bure are reveling in their win, read on for a look back at all the celebrities who pushed themselves during season five.

#877. How Hailey Bieber, Justin Bieber's Son Is Following in Dad's Footsteps

Hailey Bieber shared a new clip of her and Justin Bieber's son Jack Blues, 2, following in his footsteps by playing with a keyboard.

That's Hailey Bieber and Justin Bieber's baby, he's iconic.

The Rhode Beauty founder shared a new video of her and Justin's son Jack Blues, 2, that revealed he may already be following in the "Sorry" singer's footsteps when it comes to music.

Hailey posted a quick clip of her son on her Instagram Stories Nov. 12, showing him being mesmerized by a keyboard as he plays with the keys. In fact, zooms in on Jack's fingers in the video taken from the couch behind him as he leans against a coffee table and plays his tune while wearing a salmon-colored sweatsuit.

"I always wanted to be married and have kids and a family from a super young age," she added before demonstrating how much she loves being a mom. "Kids are just so yummy in the morning when they first wake up. They’re just so smushy."

Outside of the ballroom, Jenna Dewan is taking no critiques.

Less than a week after the Step Up alum—along with her partner Val Chmerkovskiy—was eliminated from Dancing With the Stars, she clapped back at a comment claiming she was ousted for being a “know it all.”

The video—which was deleted on Instagram but still up on TikTok—saw a viewer dancing in front of her horse stables as she shared her “hot take” that Dewan was not only a know-it-all, but also “had zero chemistry” with Chmerkovskiy and the audience because she “was so hard to relate to.”

Dewan was eliminated during the Nov. 10 episode of DWTS, a decision that many were shocked by considering she was firmly on the leaderboard throughout her nine-week run on the show.

And although The Rookie alum was visibly gutted to be sent home, she emphasized how amazing the experience had been for her.

“Dancing again, getting to share my joy with my family, who's over here every single night—thank you, my baby—I had a great time,” she said. “And I loved getting to share that with the world. Honestly, all love.”

Meanwhile, Chmerkovskiy shared some sage advice from his and Jenna Johnson’s 3-year-old son Rome in wake of the duo’s elimination.

“It’s OK to lose right?” Chmerkovskiy asked the toddler in a video shared to his Instagram Nov. 11, to which Rome replied, “Yeah, you try your best. If you don't win sometimes, you try to do it so many times.”

Chmerkovskiy admitted he was focusing on the good, telling his son, “Even though I lost and I'm sad, I feel already better because I have you in my life.”

#873. Record-breaking Ebola outbreak: phone data reconstruct first weeks of spread

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Confirmed infections of Bundibugyo Ebola have surpassed 10,000 in the DRC since May.Credit: Xinhua/Shutterstock

Epidemiologists have used mobile-phone data and test records to map the early spread of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)1 weeks before the outbreak was declared. The authors say the study findings reveal how surveillance systems failed to detect signals of the disease early on and enabled it to spread rapidly.

It is now six months since the outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain of the virus was announced. The number of confirmed infections has risen to more than 10,000 and 5,198 people have died, making this the largest Bundibugyo outbreak so far. There are no licenced vaccines or approved treatments specifically for Bundibugyo, which has complicated efforts to control it.

The DRC declared the outbreak on 15 May after laboratory tests confirmed the first case, a person from Ituri province in the country’s northeast, was infected with the Bundibugyo strain. Around the same time, suspected cases were being reported in several DRC locations, including Mongbwalu, Rwampara, Bunia and Nyankunde in Ituri, and Butembo, Katwa and Goma in the neighbouring province of North Kivu. The World Health Organization declared the outbreak a public health emergency of international concern on 17 May, citing infections among health-care workers, the geographical spread of cases and clusters of undocumented deaths. Researchers strongly suspect that the virus had been spreading in the region months earlier.

To understand how the outbreak spread so quickly, the researchers looked at anonymized mobile-phone data to trace the movement of people between areas.

Although the first confirmed case was identified on 15 May, the study reports that the person had symptoms as early as 25 April.

The team found that people travelling out of Mongbwalu, Bunia and Rwampara between 24 April and 24 May helped to predict which health zones would report infections by 1 June. For instance, areas close to the initial centres were at greater risk of infections, the study found.

The risk of infections rose again in places 150–200 kilometres away from the initial outbreak centres because people travelled to larger towns and cities along established routes, says study co-author Pierre Akilimali, an epidemiologist at the National Institute of Public Health (INSP) in Kinshasa.

The authors say the findings show that people movement was a key driver of the rapid spread in the early phases of the outbreak.

“These are very important findings which reinforce what we initially knew at the onset of the outbreak,” says Tambe Akem, an independent public-health consultant based in Yaoundé, Cameroon.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03666-z

Ebengo. D. M. et al. Science https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aej4586 (2026).

#870. The Bachelor Season 30 Lead Revealed—and Yes, He's a Catch

NFL quarterback Sam Hartman has been pulled off the proverbial bench to be the next leading man for The Bachelor season 30: “I’m excited but also very nervous.”

Just when it felt like Bachelor Nation was on the fourth down with too far to go, they clinched a Hail Mary.

Sam Hartman, a quarterback for the Washington Commanders, has been tapped to be the franchise’s next leading man on The Bachelor—a decision that fans are already praising as the perfect touchdown.

The announcement was made on Nov. 13, with Hartman admitting he was already trying to devise the perfect strategies for his Bachelor playbook. After all, wooing women is a whole different ball game for the 27-year-old.

"I’m excited but also very nervous," Hartman admitted on Good Morning America. "I have a tough time holding conversation with one girl. 30 is going to be pretty tough."

But he’s got a whole team of guys at his side hoping to help him on his journey to love—though he’s taking their guidance with a grain of turf.

“My teammates were giving me some advice on the plane ride back,” the NFL player said. “So probably not going to listen to anybody on that. But no, I'm excited.”

Thankfully, he’s got a support system much closer to home that he knows has his back: his parents and brother.

“They're excited,” he said of his family. “My mom and I have a really cool relationship, and my pops is obviously just supportive. And their big thing is just be myself and enjoy the experience, and you know, trust the instincts and trust your gut.”

The former Wake Forest Demon Deacons quarterback did admit, however, he didn’t blitz into saying yes to the franchise.

“At first I was like, ‘No way,’” he explained. “Then I got really lucky and talked to [host] Jesse Palmer, and you know he kind of gave me the insight and what it is, what it's not.’”

As he put it, “anybody in their right mind” is saying yes to being told, “‘Hey, you got a chance to go find the love of your life.’”

As for what type of woman would hit it out of the park for him?

Though Hartman said he refused to “give out all my answers right now,” he does have a general picture of the kind of personality that could win his heart.

“I think competitiveness,” he explained, “and somebody that I want to be able to chase—not chasing in a way that, like, you haven't texted me back in a week, but like chasing a way that they have a drive for something and that motivates me to wake up every day and chase them.”

Plus, with the rest of his family working in the medical field, he is always looking for “compassion,” adding, “I think that's a huge part.”

So, after Sunday Night Football ends on March 21, tune in to season 30 of The Bachelor at 8 p.m. ET on ABC, or the next day on Hulu.

Until then, read on to see where some of your favorite Bachelor Nation alums are today.

Even before Mel Owen's season of The Golden Bachelor kicked off, he was hit with a few penalties after going on the MGoBlue Podcasts With Jon Jansen and insisting, "if they’re 60 or over, I’m cutting them," adding that he wanted them to "try to stay away from the artificial hips and the wigs."

And while Peg Munson is a fellow sexagenarian, his connection with the retired firefighter and bomb tech was quite explosive, with the former NFL linebacker praising her as "high-energy" to Glamour.

Though he didn't take a knee during his November 2025 finale, the sports lawyer still offered up a Neil Lane sparkler, saying, "This represents our commitment to love, to give us time to figure out together what our future holds."

Munson announced in October 2026 that the couple had split, sharing on Instagram, "I did have to make the difficult decision to step away from the relationship. Sometimes, even when there's love, it just doesn't turn out the way that we hoped. So right now, I'm just, I'm just focusing on healing my heart and just focusing on myself, my health, and looking forward to the next chapter.”

According to Spencer Conley (who intrigued Jenn Tran with his "golden retriever energy" on The Bachelorette), he fetched quite the catch on the 10th season of Bachelor in Paradise. Posting a snippet of himself and Jess Edwards (she took a swing at Bachelor Joey Graziadei's heart) revealing that they were falling for one another—Bachelor code for I'm not quite ready to say, "I love you"—he wrote on his Instagram Stories in August 2025 that he'd "already won."

Hard same from Jess, who wrote on her main feed, "just feeling a lil giddy about this man & whatnot."

And they were certainly smiling when, after choosing their relationship over the $250,000 prize, they got engaged and walked away with a surprise check worth $190,000.

"Everything that we’ve been through," Jess said, "has led us to this exact moment."

Since then, their love led her to Dallas, Jess revealing during Mel's November 2025 After the Finale Rose special that she was Texas-bound in a few weeks.

"This was my best first date," Bailey Taylor Brown wrote on Instagram in August 2025 after she took Jeremy Simon out on Paradise's 10th season. And perhaps her last? The social media manger, who initially competed for Grant Ellis' heart, and the real estate investor who nearly charmed Bachelorette Jenn managed to survive their most dramatic squabble ever when she learned he had second thoughts about sending Susie Evans home.

Still, their connection continued to heat up in Costa Rica. And while they were sent home during the Bachelor in Paradise finale, they continued to pursue a relationship off-camera. In fact, the show revealed that they've met each other families and that they're planning to move to the same city.

"We feel so lucky to have found each other," Bailey wrote on Instagram in September 2025, "and couldn’t be more excited for what’s to come."

Seems the connection between Paradise season 10 pair Andrew Spencer (one of Katie Thurston's suitors) and Alexe Godin (from Grant's season) has remained trés strong post-show. Six days after the Chicago-based football player dubbed the pedatric speech therapist "mon amour" in an August 2025 Instagram post, she labeled him "mon chéri" in her own missive.

And while they chose love over the $250,000 prize during the BiP finale, they still got to head home with $125,000 in their pockets.

"This is frickin unreal," Alexe said. "I am leaving with money, but not just money—love, the most important thing."

And they're bringing their love to the Windy City, with the show revealing Alexe's plans to move to Chicago with Andrew.

"Finally found someone just as weird as me," she wrote on Instagram in September 2025, "and I can’t wait to do life with you."

Kat Izzo and Dale Moss went through a thorny moment during the Bachelor in Paradise finale when former contestant Sean McLaughlin alleged she "stashed a laptop" and had been sending an ex love letters. However, the nurse practitioner denied contacting him on the show.

"Did me and my ex still have a relationship prior to this?" she said. "Yes, because I didn’t think I was gonna meet anybody here."

While Kat and Dale were sent home before the final test of Paradise, their romance continued to bloom. The show revealed the alum from Zach Shallcross' season and the former contestant from Clare Crawley's went on to travel across the U.S. together and made plans to build a future together, including moving closer.

"It was tough at times," Dale commented under Kat's August 2025 Instagram post, "but we navigated it together…and I wouldn’t change a thing."

But their journey came to a close in early 2026.

Among the issues Kat detailed during a January appearance on the Bachelor Happy Hour podcast was his unwillingness to relocate from NYC.

"San Diego is apparently, to him, not anywhere he could grow his career," she explained. "I never really got full answers. I don’t really know what the true reason was."

Golden Bachelorette alum Gary Levingston and Leslie Fhima (a runner up for Golden Bachelor Gerry Turner's heart) appeared to have quite the glittery future when they were voted off Bachelor in Paradise's 10th season, even writing about "making new memories" in a post-elimination social media video. But the onetime Prince muse isn't quite sure if she wants to be his lover.

"We talk all the time," she revealed during an August 2025 appearance on Bachelor Happy Hour. "Gary is, I can honestly say right now, one of my best friends. I’ll call him if I have a problem. He kind of talks me off the ledge a little bit, and we are always there for each other. We have each other’s back."

While she acknowledged that the nearly 2,000 miles between them (she's based in Minnesota; he's in California) complicates the situation, she hasn't given up hope. "All I know is that for me, a big thing with any relationship, a romantic one for sure, is I want to be friends first," she continued. "Because I want to be with my best friend growing older."

Golden Bachelorette's head mansion man Kim Buike found someone to make sweet music with in Gerry Turner's first impression rose recipient Faith Martin. Though they were eliminated on the 10th season of Paradise, they sailed off into the sunset, with Faith posting a video to Instagram in August 2025 of the retired navy captain enjoying a hometown date with her in Washington.

However, they ultimately realized they weren't each other's person and that they were better off as friends.

"We talk sometimes two to three times a week," Faith said in a September 2025 Instagram video. "He lives five and a half hours away. But the point is this: We are not a in-love couple. Nope, we are not. We never fell in love. We had a great connection on the show."

Status: SplitGrant may have met 25 potential love interests on his first night in the Bachelor mansion, but in the end, it was Juliana Pasquarosa who scored his final rose. However, the couple decided to call it quits less than three months after their propsal aired.

“This is one of the harder things I’ve had to write, but I want to share it honestly. Juliana and I have decided to end our relationship,” Grant wrote on his Instagram Story June 13. “We both gave this our best and poured a lot of love into each other, but after a lot of deep conversations, we’ve come to the understanding that we’re simply not the right fit long term.”

Status: EngagedAfter appearing on the first-ever season of The Golden Bachelor and leaving Gerry Turner's season early, Joan Vassos handed out the roses on the debut season of The Golden Bachelorette. It was there that she met and got engaged to contestant Chock Chapple.

"We are living proof that no matter what life throws at you that there is still hope, even at our age," Joan said on The Golden Bachelorette's November 2024 finale before Chock proposed in Bora Bora. "I waited 'til this moment in this amazing location to tell you that I love you, and I want to spend the rest of my life with you. I want to wake up next to you in the morning, and I want to kiss you when I go to bed at night."

Though the pair are still navigating long-distance, they're slowly making plans for their life together.

“We have grown kids and they just happen to be falling into that part of their lives too," Joan shared in a February 2026 Instagram Q&A, explaining why they're considering a 2027 wedding date. "We'll get married sometime when our kids aren't getting married."

Status: SplitDuring the season 21 finale of The Bachelorette, it looked like The Bachelor alum Jenn Tran was finally getting her happy ending with her final pick Devin Strader. But Jenn revealed on After the Final Rose back in September 2024 that Devin gave her the cold shoulder as soon as the cameras stopped rolling.

"He was making bold proclamations of love and then suddenly the next day he was like, nothing and he denied ever being in love," Jenn told host Jesse Palmer during the Sept. 3 episode. "All the promises he had made to me, all of the love that he had wanted to give to me wasn't there anymore."

Drama continued to play out when Devin shared a 13-minute video recounting his side of the story to Instagram, where in addition to taking "accountability” he shared insight into why he ended the relationship in a 15-minute phone call.

While Jenn alleged he dumped her during the call in August, he claimed that Jenn demanded to know what was wrong as he tried to find a way to break the news in person.

"I didn't really know what else to do," he explained, noting he had been waiting to tell her in person. "She kind of forced my hand."

After that, Jenn waltzed over to Dancing With the Stars and into the heart of her partner Sasha Farber. The duo continued to dance together even after their October 2024 elimination, but split in 2025.

Status: SplitIn November 2022, Greg Grippo (one of Katie Thurston's suitors on The Bachelorette a year prior) joined Victoria Fuller on the season eight finale of Bachelor in Paradise. There, the two announced that they were in a relationship. In April 2024, he revealed the two had called it quits.

Status: SplitBefore Victoria Fuller and Greg Grippo went public with their romance on the finale of Bachelor in Paradise's eighth season, she and her costar Johnny DePhillipo ended their engagement.

Status: DivorcedGerry and Theresa Nist got engaged in November 2023 during the finale of the inaugural Golden Bachelor and tied the knot in a January 2024 televised ceremony.

However, three months after their nuptials, the couple announced that they were breaking up.

“Theresa and I have had a number of heart-to-heart conversations and we've looked closely at our situation, our living situation, so forth," Gerry said during a joint appearance on Good Morning America with Theresa April 2024. “We've come to the conclusion mutually that it's probably time for us to dissolve our marriage."

They reached a divorce settlement in June 2024, according to court records reviewed by E! News.

In April 2025, Gerry revealed on the Bachelor Happy Hour podcast that he was dating someone new and "it's going well."

#869. England respond to Jones' mind games ahead of Japan match

England scrum coach Tom Harrison denied his side will be distracted by their upcoming game against New Zealand ahead of facing Eddie Jones' Japan on Saturday at Twickenham; Cadan Murley looking to play his "best rugby" and hold down place in starting line-up

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

England have hit back at Eddie Jones' claim they could be vulnerable to an upset by Japan on Saturday because they have one eye on their upcoming game with New Zealand.

Jones is aiming to disrupt Steve Borthwick's side by hitting them with the unexpected in the belief they will be "a little bit distracted" by the All Blacks' visit to Allianz Stadium on November 21.

New Zealand are the box-office fixture of the campaign ahead of finals weekend but England deny they are looking beyond Japan.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"That's nowhere near the case because we understand how important this game is," scrum coach Tom Harrison said.

"We understand the challenge Japan can throw at us and we have to be alive in every single moment to the type of rugby they play.

"We understand that there might be unorthodox things coming our way but our need is to be alive.

"I've never worked with Eddie but I've met him a few times and he's a rugby genius, the way he thinks about the game and the way the players talk about him."

Cadan Murley wins his eighth cap but first at Twickenham after coming in for the injured Immanuel Feyi-Waboso on the left wing as one of 10 changes made for Japan.

Murley, Max Ojomoh and Will Joseph are aiming to make an impression on Borthwick after the head coach signalled that places in next year's World Cup squad are up for grabs.

"I just want go out there and play my best rugby," Murley said. "I'll focus on what I can do, control the controllables, and hopefully that will get me in the mix further down the line.

"But my sole focus is on this game and putting my best foot forward. It's my first game at Twickenham and that's what's on my mind at the moment."

#868. How do you stop Haaland? Wales show how it's done

Erling Haaland has won two Premier League titles and three Premier League Golden Boots with Manchester City

It is a question many have asked but only a few have answered successfully. How do you stop Erling Haaland?

Wales will be faced with that daunting task when they travel to Oslo on Saturday to face Norway in the Nations League.

With a record 65 goals in just 59 games for his country â not to mention the hundreds he has scored for Manchester City and his previous clubs â Haaland has conquered most defences he has encountered.

But Wales managed to shackle him during their 2-1 win in Cardiff a month ago. In that sense, they have a blueprint to keep the fearsome striker at bay.

"You're talking about trying to deal with one of the best players in his position in the world, and we've been seeing that for several years now," says Wales head coach Craig Bellamy.

"He's different to what you would normally have to deal with. He has the profile of everything you want in a player, and that's quite rare.

"It's a collective responsibility, not just an individual one."

Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC Two Wales, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Wales, Radio Cymru and 5 Live Sports Extra, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary.

Bellamy felt his team needed to take a calculated risk.

Some opponents have tried to sit back and defend deep against Haaland, but that can give him more time and space, more ways to wreak havoc.

Others have opted for a more confrontational, physical approach â not always wise against this powerful, 6ft 5in specimen.

Then there is the option of pressing high up the field. That can leave you exposed to balls over the top, which Haaland can race on to by using his raw pace.

Crucially, however, it can deny him â and, importantly, his talented team-mates â that time and space to inflict damage.

High-risk but high-reward, that is the route Bellamy chose.

"Drive up and don't let him dictate," he explains. "It's easier said than done because then you could turn around and say to me, 'Why are you playing a high line against Haaland?' Trust me you don't want to, but you can't have him dictating the game.

"That's true of all players, really, but it's much harder when someone is getting in your face and stopping you from having time on the ball.

"A good player can look like a top player if you give him time. A top player can look world-class if you give him time. A world-class player might then have a chance of looking like an ordinary or good player, if you don't allow him time.

"Putting pressure on the ball is always important for us, and I thought we did that really well that night."

Haaland was limited to 24 touches at Cardiff City Stadium. Anyone who has watched him play will know that is not unusual for the 26-year-old, who can drift in and out of a game around the pitch, only to come alive at key moments in the penalty area.

The more significant statistic is that he only had two shots, with only one on target, a header straight at Wales goalkeeper Danny Ward.

Prevention is better than a cure, and what Wales did effectively on that occasion was to cut off the supply of chances for Norway's talismanic frontman.

That was no mean feat considering that the Scandinavians' creator in chief is captain Martin Odegaard, one of the Premier League's most inventive playmakers and the man who led Arsenal to the title last season.

So as well as the defenders tasked with handling Haaland and his fellow forwards Fulham's Oscar Bobb and Andreas Schjelderup of Benfica, midfielders such as Ethan Ampadu had crucial roles to play in negating the attacking influence of Odegaard and his midfield colleagues.

"You have to consider the distance between Ethan and Haaland," Bellamy adds. "You can't open up the middle too much because balls are going to come into his feet. You have to get your distances right, be side-on and make sure you're aware of his runs.

"He has the ability to take a team on, but he also has the willingness to make those runs.

"It's also important how we use the ball. If we use it well, develop our possession and move up the pitch, he has to work. He has to run and get back."

Since Bellamy took charge in the summer of 2024, Wales' average share of possession in matches has rocketed.

They have had to make do with less of the ball in this Nations League campaign against Norway, Portugal and Denmark â and Bellamy believes his side could improve in that regard.

He has said Wales will be going "all out" for victory in Oslo on Saturday and, if they can stay on the front foot and make Norway defend, that is certainly one way of keeping Haaland out of the game.

"You have to be on it against these teams because they have many individual players who can create something out of nothing," says Dan James, who scored Wales' first goal in the 2-1 win.

"Our distances [between players] were really good. Odegaard is a unique player. He'll get the ball anywhere so it's hard as a defence. They want you to jump out and I think they showed that with their goal with the ball for Oscar Bobb and he's finished it well.

"We showed our resilience and it was about limiting their chances and I thought we did that.

"Odegaard played some great balls in behind but, to the very last minute, we defended really well, not just the defenders but the whole unit, from the forwards back.

"I thought we defended really well on the day, and we've got to be great again on Saturday."

Wales will be forced into at least one change in Oslo, with Swansea City centre-back Ben Cabango â who got Haaland's shirt after the game in Cardiff â missing through suspension.

The good news for Wales is that first-choice centre-back Joe Rodon, who was injured for the previous game, is available after returning for Leeds United last weekend.

"Ben Cabango and Ben Davies have both done really well against him [Haaland], but the work has to be done in front of them. If it isn't, you expose the defenders," Bellamy says.

"Against this type of player, it doesn't matter how good an individual defender is. We've seen over the last four or five years how difficult it becomes for one player to cope with what Haaland brings."

Taking on Haaland alone is not advisable. If you face the challenge together, however, as Wales showed just a month ago, you can stop the seemingly unstoppable.

#866. Kim Kardashian Reveals Status of Law Career After Failing Bar Exam

Kim Kardashian declared that she's "not giving up on trying to become a lawyer" over a year after failing the bar exam. The All’s Fair star has spent the last decade studying to be an attorney.

Yes, Kim Kardashian is keeping up with her lawyer aspirations.

The Kardashians star provided an update on whether she still intends on pursuing a career in law after failing the bar exam.

"I'm not giving up on trying to become a lawyer," Kardashian told Good Morning America on the red carpet at the All’s Fair season two premiere on Nov. 2. "I think that that was like a big misconception, but I do want to wait until the timing is right so that I know that I can do it without a ton of distractions around me."

"I don't know when that will be," she continued, "because there's always distractions. But it means a lot to me and I want to do it—and I'm gonna do it!"

The 46-year-old—who joked about failing the bar exam in an energy drink ad this past summer—had previously explained why she was so open about not getting the results she wanted on the test after completing a six-year law program.

"You get the results on a Friday, and I knew Sunday morning they were going to be live on the internet," she told the New York Times last December. "I was like, 'OK, let's do this, I know what I've got to do. This really sucks because I put so much time into it, but I know what I can do better.'"

The SKIMS founder continued, "I'm pretty good at taking a failure and turning it into something and I just don't have the time to dwell. You can feel sorry for yourself for a second, but I need to take that time and put it into studying more."

That said, she did have to take a short moment to privately process her results before making them public.

"I didn't feel good about it," Kardashian explained. "I was really uncomfortable and not confident for a while."

She's also always been clear about her intentions of following through with her lawyer aspirations. (Her late dad Robert Kardashian Sr. was an attorney.)

"Falling short isn't failure—it's fuel," she wrote on her Instagram Stories in Nov. 2025, after announcing her bar exam results. "I was so close to passing the exam and that only motivates me even more."

Kardashian's interest in becoming a lawyer is just one of the many career paths she's taken. Keep reading for more about her evolution over the years...

#865. EFL warns clubs over social media posts

The English Football League (EFL) has warned its members about their usage of posts on social media that might target other sides regarding disciplinary issues.

In September, Wrexham aimed a Spygate-based dig at Southampton in a video that featured their owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney in a cheeky social media post.

This came before the Dragons played Saints, eventually winning the Championship game 2-1 at the Racecourse Ground.

Wrexham's owners appeared on Wrexham's X account, which started with Reynolds emerging from behind a tree.

A few weeks later, Southampton fired back at Wrexham after the Welsh club had been fined by the EFL for fielding two ineligible players.

Saints commented "hope you've double checked this one lads" on their X account under Wrexham's team news post for a following game against Sheffield United.

Birmingham City also joined in with the Spygate themed posts, with a graphic of both clubs' badges cut into grass hedges, shown through the eye of binoculars before playing each other in September.

The EFL has since sent a letter to club chairs and executives, advising clubs to avoid posts that could have a reputational impact.

#864. Pochettino’s Chelsea maelstrom the best yardstick for what lies ahead at United

Argentinian oversaw high-scoring games in his one Chelsea season and Opta predicts his Manchester United side will move upfield quicker than that team

Among the 20 managers with more than 290 matches in the Premier League, only the five “big beasts” of Alex Ferguson, Arsène Wenger, José Mourinho, Jürgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola have better points-per-game averages than Mauricio Pochettino. He is an elite manager.

Pochettino took over Southampton midway through their first season back in the top flight (2012-13) after the club spent seven years in the lower leagues. In his only full campaign, they finished eighth. He led Tottenham to second in 2016-17, third in the seasons either side, and reached the 2019 Champions League final. His presence lifted those clubs.

However, the Argentinian has competed in only one of the past six Premier League campaigns. Winning Ligue 1 and the Coupe de France in an 18-month spell with Paris Saint-Germain tells us little. His most pertinent recent experience for the Manchester United job is the 2023-24 season he spent at Chelsea, a campaign that left more questions than answers.

The club had finished 12th the season before, in the first year of the Todd Boehly/Clearlake Capital era. Pochettino was always likely to take Chelsea higher. And he did. But his influence is harder to judge. Opta predicted Chelsea would finish sixth in 2023-24, a forecast that proved correct. By this measure Pochettino hit par though, as Transfermarkt rated the market value of his squad as the third-highest in the Premier League in October 2023, perhaps he fell short.

The squad value grew thanks to remarkable investment. Chelsea spent more than any other club in Europe’s big five leagues in each of the three transfer windows from the summer of 2022 to the summer of 2023. Working for Boehly will have provided a good primer for the madness of Manchester United, even if the spending won’t be as generous.

Assembling a winning team from a rapidly evolving squad is not easy. Pochettino crafted a side that delivered the fifth-most expected points in 2023-24. Chelsea’s 63.4 was a fair way shy of Arsenal (81.2), Manchester City (79.3) and Liverpool (76.2) but it was a decent first season.

Chelsea conceded 63 league goals, the club’s worst figure in the Premier League era. Yet only twice have they amassed more than the 77 goals they scored. They were a little above their expected goal figures at each end but the bulk of their large goal totals was reflected in the underlying data.

But even the xG numbers raised questions, because Chelsea benefited from 12 penalties, the joint-second-most in the past 10 Premier League seasons. Chelsea have had 14 in their 86 league games since Pochettino left. They conceded five penalties and committed the joint-most Opta-defined defensive errors leading to shots (22) in Pochettino’s season.

Across three matches in April 2024 they drew 2-2 with the bottom side Sheffield United, thumped Everton 6-0 then lost 5-0 at Arsenal. They endured a similar seesaw sequence earlier in the campaign, losing 4-1 at Tottenham and Newcastle, with a 4-4 draw against Manchester City in between. Chelsea also set the record for matches in which a team score and concede at least two goals in a 38-game Premier League season (12). How do you assess a manager’s performance in that maelstrom?

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

If the low point was not the Arsenal loss, it was being called “billion-pound bottle jobs” by Gary Neville after losing the 2024 Carabao Cup final. Never mind that Chelsea had enough chances to win, Pochettino had to answer for the defeat. Less than three months later, he was gone.

The Premier League has evolved in Pochettino’s relatively brief absence. Arne Slot arrived, won the title and left, while Guardiola’s departure leaves no big managerial beasts remaining. There have been tactical shifts, with increased man-to-man marking across the pitch, and set-piece skirmishes have decided more matches than feels healthy.

Opta’s data shows Pochettino’s probable new side move upfield more quickly but press less intensely than his Chelsea team. There will need to be an adjustment. But can a manager whose training methods at Chelsea were described by a well-placed source as “antiquated” get up to speed as quickly as United need?

Pochettino will adapt and his Premier League record commands the utmost respect. The relevance of his recent work to United in 2026-27 is less clear.

#863. Christian Cousins, Kindergarten Cop Actor, Dead at 43

Christian Cousins, a former child actor who starred alongside Arnold Schwarzenegger in Kindergarten Cop, died at 43 in October, his brother shared.

Christian Cousins—who starred alongside Arnold Schwarzenegger in Kindergarten Cop in the ‘90s—died in October, his brother Jonas Roeser confirmed on social media. He was 43.

“It’s hard to share that my brother, Christian Cousins, has passed away,” Jonas captioned an Oct. 22 Instagram post, within which he noted that he connected with Christian and his twin brother Joseph Cousins later in life. “They grew up in California while I was in Washington and I didn’t get to know them until I was in college. Before that, I grew up watching them on television in Knots Landing and the lead role of Dominic in Kindergarten Cop with Arnold Schwarzenegger.”

“But those roles are only a small part of how I’ll remember Christian,” Jonas continued. “He was a character, full of passion and energy, with big stories and even bigger dreams.”

He noted that Christian had been battling liver disease, though he did not share additional information.

“It brings me comfort to believe he is now in heaven with his mother, free from the pain he was carrying,” Jonas concluded. “Rest easy, Christian. I hope your soul is at rest and that you’ve found peace. You are my brother and you will be missed.”

Christian and his twin Joseph shared the role of Dominic in the 1990 film Kindergarten Cop, which saw Arnold play LAPD detective John Kimble, who is forced to go undercover as a kindergarten teacher.

In addition to the beloved film, Christian appeared in the series Knot’s Landing as Bobby Gibson Ewing, again sharing the role with Joseph, and had credits on 1991’s Critters 3, 1992’s Intruders and Twin Sitters in 1994.

He pivoted away from acting, however, and in 2020­—during a virtual reunion with Arnold and the cast of Kindergarten Cop—revealed an executive for a furniture business and co-owned a CBD company.

During the conversation, Arnold expressed his disbelief to see the cast of the series so grown up, noting, “It is the funniest thing to see all of you guys.”

Christian, for his part, had some thank yous to extend to the Terminator actor, courtesy of his character Dominic.

“By the way, after 30 years I want to thank you again for saving my life from Richard Tyson in the locker room,” Christian said in reference to the film, adding of the fact Detective Kimble ends up with his onscreen mother, “And I’m glad you ended up with my mom for that movie. That was awesome.”
